title: Hand Phaser Type I
subtitle: Standard field equipment
summary: The palm-sized sidearm: a gloss-black shell with an antimony face plate around the photon emitter, a cross-hatched electron aspirator pile on top, and the force wheel and indicator dial beside the operational light.
description: The smallest phaser, carried alone or locked into the Type II pistol. Five effective ranges are printed on the sheet, from heat to overload.
interpretation: Plan and depth profiles follow the sheet’s body lines and sections. The lattice of the aspirator pile, the dial markings and the gloss finish are simplified.

title: Hand Phaser Type II
subtitle: Standard field equipment
summary: The pistol assembly with a Type I locked on top, as the sheet requires. In front are the topaz beam shield and emitter and the knurled photon accelerator. The blue-grey body carries the dilithium crystal cell, and the grip is raked back with S/T firing triggers.
description: A long-range pistol built around the Type I. The printed overall width of 49.40 mm equals the Type I’s own width, which confirms the two are dimensioned as one assembly.
components: Firing triggers: S = safety, T = trigger
interpretation: The side profile and grip rake come from the lines-and-sections sheet (PDF 105). The grip’s cross-section between stations, the accelerator knurl count and the lockplate recesses are simplified.

title: Ray Gun
sizeBasis: printed length overall; printed maximum diameter
subtitle: Offensive/defensive area weapon
summary: A turned grey body housing that tapers to a rounded tail. An antimony collette steps up to the translucent diamond emitter tube, and a split antimony trigger strip on top selects offensive or defensive fire.
description: An area weapon. Its printed effective areas (3 m at 90 m, 8 m at 180 m) describe a widening field rather than a beam.
interpretation: The broken-out side view and the circular front view both show a round body, so it is modelled as a solid of revolution. Its radii are measured on the plan at the 0–5 cm bar.

title: Communicator
sizeBasis: printed W.O.A × L.O.A × H.O.A, checked on the closed pose
subtitle: Standard field equipment item
summary: Upper and lower black shells meet at a gold band. The perforated antenna grille is shown flipped open on its hinge, uncovering the LEDs, the transmit/receive and channel switches and the vent.
description: A 200-gram field communicator rated to 12,000 km, powered by an 006P energy unit.
interpretation: Closed, it measures the printed 113.5 × 63.5 × 28 mm. The grille swings out past vertical, about 110°, as the sheet’s dash-dot “antenna open” outline shows, and the layout of the switches under the grille is interpreted from callouts the sheet draws only through the perforations.

title: Ear Receiver
sizeBasis: printed width overall; printed maximum diameter; printed length overall
subtitle: For non-public reception
summary: A finned antimony receiver housing over a black core, with an energy cell and high-gain antenna grid at the base. On top, the earphone and transparent custom-moulded ear-piece swivel stiffly at about 40°.
description: A closed-loop receiver for all prime subspace channels, used where transmissions are private or the surroundings are noisy.
components: High gain antenna grid and heat sink
interpretation: The ear-piece is moulded to each user’s ear, so its shape here is generic. The sheet marks 40° on the plan without saying what it is measured from (the drawn housing axis measures ≈35°), so the swivel is posed between the two. The drawing measures about 3% longer than the printed 6.55 cm, and the model follows the drawing.

title: Universal Translator
sizeBasis: printed maximum diameter; printed length overall
subtitle: U.F.P. standard
summary: A long antimony cylinder. At the front are the raked speech-sensor block and the knurled decoding/encoding ring. Along the top run the computer functions display under its transparent cover and the operator’s speaker grille, and the activating switch sits at 45° near the data storage banks.
description: Used to talk with Federation members and with unknown alien language forms in the treaty exploration territory.
interpretation: The display panel’s lit cells form an illustrative pattern, not a readout from the sheet. All other proportions are measured at the sheet’s 0–6 cm bar.

title: Sciences Tricorder
sizeBasis: printed W.O.A × D.O.A; height with display head raised measured on PDF 113 (printed closed height 177.8 mm)
subtitle: Type I
summary: Shown in the open arrangement. The display-control head is raised to expose the video display, sensor array, three indicator lights and three selector knobs. Below are the eight removable record/play discs and the speaker/mic, and the circuitry section stays closed.
description: Senses, measures, analyses, compares and identifies the surrounding environment, with multi-channel recording and a choice of display modes.
components: Disc selector / channel selector / record-play controls
interpretation: Every side view shows the open head swung back on its pivot (roughly 30–45°; no angle is printed). This study keeps it upright as the front views draw it, so the head-raised height is a front-view figure. Olive and black can’t be told apart in the halftone, so the case is shown black. The 127 cm strap is shown only by its lugs, and the speaker grille’s concentric-arc pattern and the sensor lattice are simplified. The 1.27 mm frame wall is from the PDF 113 section; PDF 114 separately prints a 2.54 mm frame.

title: Medical Tricorder
sizeBasis: printed W.O.A × D.O.A; height with display head raised measured on PDF 125; depth not compared (lower lid drawn partially open)
subtitle: Standard field equipment item — Type I
summary: The medical variant shares the sciences case. Its open arrangement adds the life-form functions sensor/analyzer bay and a lower compartment lid drawn partly open; LEDs A–C and controls D–F sit beside the video display.
description: A 900-gram field diagnostic unit with 24-channel capability. The sheet notes that its internal circuitry is classified.
interpretation: As on the sciences unit, the open head is kept upright although the side views show it swung back on its pivot. The analyzer is shown in olive to set it apart, since the halftone doesn’t settle its colour. The lower lid is swung out 14° to show “partially open”, and the hidden internal arrangement is interpreted. The strap is shown only by its lugs, and the speaker grille is simplified.

title: Heartbeat Reader
sizeBasis: printed maximum diameter; printed length overall
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: Shaped like a microphone. A spherical guard and ground-plane screen, joined by a clamp band, enclose the omnidirectional sensor. The body carries the BPM readout, two indicators and the activate/audible slide switches, and the base holds the sample and volume selector.
description: Reads the heartbeats of one or many life forms at once. By cancelling known individuals one at a time, it can pick out an alien disguised within a group.
components: Guard and anti-stray audible noise screen
interpretation: The screen mesh is drawn as a coarse wire lattice. The printed length is about 1% longer than the drawing, so the vertical measurements are scaled to meet it.

title: Spray Applicator
sizeBasis: printed maximum diameter; printed length overall (loaded)
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: A transparent, fluted pressurised vial on an antimony applicator body. The spray trigger is pressed from the side, and an interchangeable nozzle is fitted at the base.
description: Applies external medications, antibiotics and protective dressings to small wounds and contusions.

specs.label: Nozzles (orifice dia.)
specs.value: Extra fine .0025 · fine .025 · medium .20 mm · coarse special order

colourKey.name: Antimony (basic; otherwise matches the vial contents’ colour code)

interpretation: The vial is shown clear because colour follows its contents, which vary.

title: Medical Scanner
sizeBasis: printed maximum diameter; printed length overall
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: A grey computer housing with eight flutes. Its top dial reads six emission groups against the normal Terran range. Below the collar, the rotating scanner turns inside a 48-mesh screen above the ground-plane screen and life-form scale.
description: Assesses the general medical condition of intelligent life forms by sensing body emanations in alpha, beta, gamma, Kirlian, theta and xi groups.

specs.label: Reading groups
specs.value: A, B, Γ, K, Θ, Ξ

components: (E) Readings dial (increase from bottom to top)
interpretation: The 48-mesh screen is shown translucent so the rotating scanner can be seen through it. The scanner’s exact shape and the dial’s bar readings are illustrative, and the tiny letters on the life-form scale are illegible in the scan.

title: Anabolic Protoplaser
sizeBasis: printed size-2 length and height (the study shows size 0 and size 2 side by side; width not compared)
subtitle: Portable wound healer
summary: The minor-injury size 0 (left) and the massive-injury size 2 (right). Size 0 has a grey housing on a black removable bottom panel and tapers to a pointed ray emission duct. Size 2 is all grey, with a side activating switch (black off / red on), an effectivity-sensor nub at the front, and a DNA match unit that flares into a blunt cylinder with a recessed duct.
description: Standard field wound healers in two sizes. The larger unit runs up to 500 EmV/AU².
interpretation: Each size is modelled from its own sheet: size 0 at 44 px/cm on PDF 130 and size 2 at 34 px/cm on PDF 131. Section shapes between the drawn views and the depth of the recessed duct are interpreted.

title: Surgical Scalpels
sizeBasis: no dimensions printed; MK10-0 height and body diameter measured at the sheet's 0–4 cm bar; three models side by side
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: Three laser scalpels in rodinium housings. A ribbed surgeon’s grip carries the intensity scale, trigger and range scale lock under a prime-focus cone, which grows taller and blunter as cutting width increases.
description: Cutting widths of 1, 2 and 3 AU. Intensity falls from 0–80 to 0–70 EmV/AU² as the width increases.
interpretation: The sheet prints no dimensions; all sizes are measured at its 0–4 cm bar.
